questions.q: How often do work-related heat illnesses move from report to accepted and paid WICA claim?
questions.have: Heat is recognised and benefit types are published; heat-specific process counts were not verified. [S13, S14, S15]
questions.could: Secure aggregate reporting of notified, filed, accepted and paid claims with time intervals and broad worker categories.
questions.scale: Illustrative: all available cases across several hot seasons; no individual case details published.

questions.q: Does PCP access reduce total costs and delayed care during hot periods for covered migrant workers?
questions.have: A patient-experience survey exists, without a heat-specific causal comparison. [S17]
questions.could: Prospective hot-season facility and worker survey with pre-specified comparison periods, full care costs and aggregate results.
questions.scale: Illustrative: 10-15 clinics; final size based on expected heat case volume.

questions.q: How consistently do workers receive and use paid heat-rest breaks?
questions.have: Official guidance recognises specified breaks as paid work; implementation outcomes were not verified. [S14]
questions.could: Confidential worker and employer survey plus aggregate work-schedule observations across heat levels, without individual tracking.
questions.scale: Illustrative: 40-60 worksites across several exposed sectors.

questions.q: Which access steps explain non-receipt of temporary support during heat-related household income loss?
questions.have: National ComCare receipt counts and assisted-application routes exist. [S1, S29]
questions.could: Representative repeated household survey measuring awareness through on-time receipt, including explicit residency eligibility checks.
questions.scale: Illustrative: 1,500-2,000 households over two hot seasons.
